rows.title: Automated terminal activation kills all running tasks in terminals
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the report and for confirming the workaround. Command-based activation is intentionally the default because it can activate environments in any shell; `shellStartup` is the non-disruptive opt-in for supported shells, and `off` is available where no automatic activation is wanted. The same Ctrl+C behavior was subsequently reviewed and closed as designed in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-python-environments/issues/1570. Please continue using `"python-envs.terminal.autoActivationType": "shellStartup"` for this workflow.

rows.title: IndentationError when executing nested for-loops via “Run Selection/Line in Python Terminal”
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the report. This is covered by https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-python/issues/25937, which tracks the same macOS regression where Run Selection/Line sends multi-line Python incorrectly and produces indentation or syntax errors. That command is implemented by the core Python extension, so consolidating there will keep the investigation with the owning code; this report adds useful evidence that nested loops fail both line-by-line and cell-by-cell.
rows.verifyEvidence: A's IndentationError triggers on nested for-loop blocks with no size or shell-integration evidence; B is a macOS chunking defect on large flat selections tied to python.terminal.shellIntegration.enabled — different trigger chains sharing one error.

rows.title: What is the global environment for?
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the context. A manager extension should keep a project selection project-scoped rather than also changing the global interpreter; consumers should subscribe to `pythonEnvsApi.onDidChangeEnvironment` and use the legacy `api.environments.onDidChangeActiveEnvironmentPath` only as a fallback when the Python Environments extension is unavailable. This is also the maintainer guidance recorded in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-python-environments/issues/1491#issuecomment-4383115486, and dedicated support has since landed for ty in https://github.com/astral-sh/ty-vscode/pull/406 and been tracked for Ruff at https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff-vscode/issues/1029. For further Python-in-VS-Code usage questions, please use https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-python/discussions/categories/q-a.

[Python Environments] default value of python-envs.workspaceSearchPaths is not respected
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the report and follow-up. The current default is intentionally `[".venv", "*/.venv"]`, which searches the workspace root and one folder level; the recursive `./**/.venv` default was removed in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-python-environments/pull/1419 because of discovery-performance risks. The linked documentation is therefore stale and should be corrected. `python-envs.globalSearchPaths` supports absolute user-level locations, but it does not cover your request for one workspace-relative recursive pattern across every repository, so this should remain open for an area-owner decision on that capability.

rows.title: Kernel crashes when using a Pixi environment with Python Environments enabled
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the detailed report and control tests. This is the Windows kernel-crash variant of the Pixi activation problem tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-python-environments/issues/1672: the registered `pixi shell` command does not return for the chained environment-variable probe, causing the same 30-second timeout already associated with kernel exit code `0xC06D007F` on Windows. Consolidating there; the Windows setup, path containing spaces, Matplotlib trigger, two timed-out probes, and exit code from this report are useful additional evidence for the fix.
rows.verifyEvidence: Both hit the pixi-shell activation timeout, but A's defect is the kernel dying after successful start (exit 3228369023 on matplotlib import); B tracks only a 30s startup stall, so A's crash would go untracked.
